result.title: Looking Right Is Not Being Right: Evaluating the Geometry of Agent-Built 3D Scenes
result.summary: Vision-language agents can reconstruct rooms from video as editable 3D scenes, but convincing renders do not establish geometric accuracy. We introduce a scan-referenced evaluation and use controlled experiments to study reconstruction accuracy, the role of geometric inputs, and agents' ability to verify and correct their scenes. Our geometric score measures surface, depth, and furniture placement agreement with laser scans of 30 real rooms on a 0-100 scale. The strongest tested agent, GPT-6 Astra, scores 51.4 from video alone, while a dense reconstruction from the same video scores 75.9. Given the point cloud used for that reconstruction, Astra produces an editable scene that scores within three points of it. Agents also inherit input errors: rescaling the supplied geometry changes scene scale almost proportionally. During revision, viewing renders improves appearance more consistently than geometry. Logs of their tool calls show that agents repeatedly measure their inputs but rarely compare them with the scenes they build. To provide this missing check, we introduce a geometric error report that compares each saved scene with the agent's input points and lists the largest discrepancies. Without new geometric evidence, the report raises the revision gains of GPT-6.1 Terra and Sol by 3.9 and 5.5 points over concurrent controls.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出以激光扫描为参照的几何评分（曲面、深度、家具布局，0–100 分），在 30 个真实房间上评测视觉语言智能体由视频构建可编辑 3D 场景的几何准确度，并分析几何输入的作用、智能体的自我核查与修订行为，以及一种对照输入点云的几何误差报告能否提升修订收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 的视觉证据筛选和验证环节相关：结果显示渲染图自检主要改善外观而非几何，误差报告迫使智能体比对输入与已建场景后才提升修订增益，可供核查「看哪里」与「是否验证了任务必要几何信息」之间的差距。
